summary.tldr: Changes Criminal Code bail rules for some serious violent and firearms offences, and adds a review of the new and amended provisions.
what_it_does: Creates a reverse onus rule for people charged with a serious violent offence involving a weapon if they were convicted in the last five years of a similar offence.
Adds certain firearms offences to the existing reverse onus rules.
Expands the intimate partner violence reverse onus rule so it also applies when the accused was previously discharged for that offence.
Requires courts to consider any previous convictions involving violence and to record that community safety and security were considered.
Provides for a parliamentary review of the new and amended provisions to begin on the fifth anniversary of royal assent, or as soon as possible after that.
who_it_affects: People charged with serious violent offences
People accused of intimate partner violence
summary.background: The bill was introduced in the House of Commons on 16 May 2023 and had first reading. It amends the Criminal Code and makes consequential amendments to other Acts.
